title: Khara and Dushana
hook: the sages and the gods gather in the sky to watch one man stand in front of an army

segments.voice: Yesterday: Khara and Dushana, part one. Fourteen thousand marched, and Rama sent Sita and Lakshmana to a cave to face them alone. Did you take on a hard thing for someone? Day five hundred sixty-four.

Rama puts on his armor, strings his bow, and waits outside the empty hut. Valmiki says the sages, the gods and the celestial beings gather in the sky above Janasthana to watch. Some of them are worried. One man against fourteen thousand. They pray for him aloud. Then the dust rises on the horizon, the drums get louder, and the army of Khara comes into view, a dark mass like storm clouds rolling in.
screen: `ARMOR ON, BOW STRUNG.` → `THE GODS WATCH FROM THE SKY.` → `AN ARMY LIKE STORM CLOUDS.`

segments.voice: The battle fills several chapters, and Valmiki tells it in detail. Rama's arrows fly so fast, he says, that the rakshasas can't see him draw or release, only the bow bending into a circle. The army falls back, regroups, and charges again. Dushana leads one assault and falls. Trishiras, the three-headed, comes next, and falls too. Then only Khara is left, and the fight between the two of them is fierce. Khara cuts Rama's bow, shatters his armor. Rama takes up another bow and goes on. Khara even tears up a tree and hurls it. Before the end, the two exchange taunts, and Rama names what Khara has done: the sages he has terrorized, the hermits killed in the forest. Finally Rama fits an arrow and Khara falls. The text says it was all over in a muhurta and a half, a little over an hour. The gods rain flowers. The sages come down and praise him. Then Lakshmana comes out of the cave with Sita, and Sita, seeing Rama alive, unhurt, surrounded by grateful sages, runs and holds him. A few days ago, Rama promised the sages to protect them. Sita asked whether that promise was wise. Today the promise is kept, at full cost, by one person. But one rakshasa, Valmiki says, slipped away from the field. His name is Akampana. And he's heading south, toward the sea, toward Lanka.
screen: `THE BOW BENT INTO A CIRCLE.` · `DUSHANA FALLS, THEN TRISHIRAS.` · `KHARA AND RAMA, ALONE.` · `SITA RUNS TO HIM.` · then, large: `ONE ESCAPES TO LANKA.`

segments.voice: Sit and let your body be still and alert. Think of a promise you made that turned out to be harder to keep than you expected. Picture yourself keeping it, or keeping the part of it you still can. Notice any tiredness that comes up, and breathe into it. A kept promise doesn't need to be dramatic. It just needs to be kept. Rest in that for the sit. The bell holds the time.
Khara and Dushana. Rama alone defeats their army at Janasthana, keeping his promise to the sages. One rakshasa escapes to Lanka.
Your line: Khara and Dushana. Today, keep one promise that's become harder than you thought. Day five hundred sixty-four.

howItsDone: The battle of Janasthana is told in many Ramlila performances, and devotees often point to it as the moment Rama's promise to the forest sages is fulfilled.

fork.setup: you're Khara. your army is gone and Rama's bow is cut. what do you do?
options: fight on alone: tear up a tree and hurl it.
fork.reveal: Khara fights to the end, even hurling a tree, until Rama's arrow brings him down.

original.note: Sanskrit muhūrta: a traditional unit of time, about 48 minutes. the battle takes one and a half, a little over an hour.

trapdoor: what you thought: this is just one more battle.
what it means: it's the promise to the sages kept, by Rama alone.
what a scholar hears: Aranya 25–30 end with Khara's death; the survivor Akampana carries the news to Ravana in Aranya 31.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Aranya Kanda 25–30 (the battle; Dushana, Trishiras and Khara fall; Sita embraces Rama)
Valmiki Ramayana, Aranya Kanda 31 (Akampana escapes to Lanka)

notes: 'A little over an hour' renders 'a muhurta and a half' (1.5 x 48 minutes = 72 minutes; some editions differ); confirm.
Khara cutting Rama's bow and breaking his armor, and hurling a tree: confirm in Aranya 28–30.
The arrow that kills Khara is said in some editions to be one given by Agastya; left unspecified here.

Audit (second sample): corrected the battle's length: a muhurta and a half is about 72 minutes, not 'about an hour and a half' (teach, myth reveal and original note); removed the stock line 'here's the thing to notice' and 'the battle is long', which clashed with the short time.
